#+TITLE: Fixtures Designed But Not Built
#+AUTHOR: Daniel Okuniewicz Jr.
#+DATE: 2026-08-23

* Designed 2026-08-23, to be built next session

Each entry below is a fixture this tree *needs* and does not have, with what it
pins and how to build it. They came out of reading the GeoPackage Encoding
Standard's normative SQL (OGC 12-128r19, Annex C and the extension annexes)
against what this crate writes -- see =handoff.org= § BUGS FOUND entries 16--18
and =plans/same-format-fidelity.org= § THE DEFECTS, defect 6.

*Read =HOSTILE.org= first* for the naming rules and the standing requirement
that every fixture be *confirmed readable by geosetta without error* before it
is committed.

*** BUILT 2026-08-23: =spec_conformant.gpkg=
/The entry that stood at the top of this file -- "the one that matters most" --
has been built and is documented in =HOSTILE.org= under the new =spec_= prefix./
Its DDL is transcribed mechanically from the annexes at a *pinned commit*
(=fe83fdd=), by =tests/fixtures/build_spec_fixtures.sh=, which starts from an
empty file rather than from =gdal_hostile.gpkg= the way
=build_sqlite_fixtures.sh= does -- that difference is the entire point of it.

It closed the substring-assertion gap it was designed for.
=the_registry_ddl_is_what_the_standard_says= compares *whole normalised DDL*
per table, and =MasterObject= gained a =sql= field so that comparison could be
written at all. **All six registry tables this crate emits match the
standard exactly**, so the 2026-08-23 spec pass holds up under a check that
does not depend on anyone remembering what to assert.

** =gpkg_metadata_autoincrement.gpkg= -- /narrowed 2026-08-23; still worth building/
=gpkg_metadata= is specified as =id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT=, so a
populated one *requires a =sqlite_sequence= row*.

***Two thirds of this entry was already covered and nobody had checked.***
=gdal_hostile.gpkg= and =sqlite_contents.gpkg= both carry a =gpkg_metadata=
that declares AUTOINCREMENT with a live =sqlite_sequence= row, so "a populated
=gpkg_metadata= needs a sequence row" needed no new fixture at all -- it needed
somebody to run =SELECT * FROM sqlite_sequence= against the fixtures already
here. The gap itself was closed on 2026-08-23 without this file.

*What is still uncovered, and it is the sharp part:* in every fixture in this
tree the mark **equals** =max(id)=. The state that distinguishes a high-water
mark from a recomputable maximum -- a mark *above* =max(id)=, left behind by a
deleted row -- appears nowhere. Until it does, a carrying implementation that
recomputed the mark from the rows would pass every test here.

*Build:* =sqlite3=, the Metadata extension's DDL, two rows, then delete the
second. That leaves =seq= at 2 with =max(id)= of 1.

*Build:* =sqlite3=, the Metadata extension's DDL, two rows, then delete one so
the high-water mark exceeds =max(id)= -- which is the only state that makes
the sequence row observable rather than derivable.

** =gpkg_tiles.gpkg=
A real tile pyramid: several tiles across two zoom levels, with complete
=gpkg_tile_matrix_set= and =gpkg_tile_matrix= rows.

*Pins:* D8 -- a tile pyramid is *carried*, as independent container content,
and no file is rejected for holding one. =sqlite_contents.gpkg= carries a
*minimal* one row deep, enough to pin bug 14's reporting; it is not enough to
test *carrying*, which has to move real BLOB payloads across the rewrite.

*Build:* =gdal_translate -of GPKG= over a small raster, or =sqlite3= directly
from the tiles DDL. /Prefer GDAL here/ -- unlike the registry DDL above, the
tile *data* is exactly the case where a real producer's output is what occurs.

** =gpkg_range_constraints.gpkg=
Two =gpkg_data_column_constraints= rows of =constraint_type = 'range'=, which
both have =value= NULL by definition -- =value= is for =enum= and =glob=.

*Pins:* an assumption a carrying implementation will otherwise make.
=CONSTRAINT gdcc_ntv UNIQUE (constraint_name, constraint_type, value)= **does
not make range rows unique**, because SQLite treats NULLs as distinct under
UNIQUE. /Measured 2026-08-23, by accident:/ an
=INSERT INTO ... SELECT * FROM ... LIMIT 1= against a real file duplicated a
=price_range= row and the UNIQUE index accepted it. Anything that dedupes on
that key, or assumes the index makes a set, is wrong.

** =sqlite_pagesize.gpkg= and =sqlite_reserved.gpkg=
The last two =sqlite.rs= gaps, neither of which any fixture reaches: a page
size other than 4096 (the writer hardcodes =WRITE_PAGE_SIZE=), and non-zero
reserved per-page space (the reader computes =usable_size= from header byte 20;
the writer always assumes zero).

*Build:* =PRAGMA page_size = 8192= before creating any table, and a
=PRAGMA reserved_bytes=-equivalent build for the second (SQLite exposes this
only via a VFS or =sqlite3_file_control=; failing that, patch header byte 20 by
hand and re-checksum nothing -- SQLite has no page checksums by default).

*Pins:* that a same-format run is *content*-preserving rather than
byte-preserving, which is currently a claim in the plan with nothing behind it.

* WHAT IS ALREADY COVERED, SO NOBODY REBUILDS IT
- =WITHOUT ROWID= -- =sqlite_altered.gpkg=, and its rows are now *counted*
  rather than reported as uncountable.
- =ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN= short records with a =DEFAULT= -- same fixture.
- =UNIQUE=, =TEXT PRIMARY KEY=, an explicit =CREATE INDEX=, and a
  =UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE= -- =sqlite_constraints.gpkg=.
- A =data_type='attributes'= registration and a minimal tile registration --
  =sqlite_contents.gpkg=.
- Index cells past the on-page ceiling, so overflow chains -- *not a fixture*
  but =sqlite::tests::an_index_btree_survives_a_write_at_every_depth= and the
  =#[ignore]=d =sqlite_itself_validates_the_index_this_writer_builds=, both of
  which build their records in-test. /Added 2026-08-23, after the first version
  of both used uniformly short keys and never reached =write_overflow= at
  all -- the "unadventurous values" blind spot, for the third time./
